comments.text:
Reopened: > *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Confirmed supervision regression: record-distribution HTTP errors lose details

API-009 explicitly requires preserving HTTP status and decoded/raw body details, including endpoint-specific error data. At 65d8e58 (unchanged by the subsequent documentation-only repair), check_distribution/4 collapses 401, 404, and 504 responses into atoms. This is a newly introduced operation, so the compatibility exception for existing legacy mappings does not justify those new information-losing branches.

The controller reproduced the defect through the real function with an offline example.invalid adapter: HTTP 504 with {"message":"distribution check failed","details":["edge unavailable"]} returns {:error, :timeout} instead of retaining status and the complete body. The expected status/body contract fails. No live API call was made and no library source was edited during reproduction.

Use the shared status/body-preserving error convention for these responses and correct the existing tests that currently assert information loss. Cover 401/404/504 with decoded bodies lacking conventional keys and raw bodies as relevant. Retain the existing successful boolean result, one-shot request, input validation, transport failures, and caller Req configuration. Do not change the legacy zone-level distribution operation's established error mapping. Demonstrate failure-before/success-after and all approved DoD gates before closing this same issue again.

This verified rework is expedited to priority 1 ahead of new API work; the existing severity, category, campaign, track, and ready-for-agent labels remain unchanged. This is repair of the approved issue, not new scope.

Reopened: > *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Supervision regression: nil sort entries bypass validation

CORE-007 is not yet fully satisfied. At completed commit 6a272223176ade5135d826679441c8e38c03c4c8, the exact committed validate_sort/2 and private predicate bodies return ok for [nil], [nil, name: :sideways], and [nil, :unsupported]. A four-case isolated ExUnit reproduction has three failures and a passing valid/non-nil control. The latest completed ReqDnsimple changes do not alter this validator.

The cause is conclusive and local: Enum.find/2 returns nil both when it finds the invalid nil entry and when no invalid entry exists; the subsequent nil branch accepts the input. A leading nil therefore also prevents later bad entries from being checked. No network, application-state, or environment hypothesis is needed. The reproduction compiled only the exact pure helper bodies from the immutable snapshot in a separate Elixir VM; no Mix command or active-worktree source edit was used.

Required follow-up: add regression cases to the real sort tests for nil alone and nil followed by an invalid direction/field, across all applicable list entry points. Each must return a NimbleOptions validation error before HTTP or serialization. Preserve existing valid keyword and atom shorthand behavior. Use an unambiguous tagged validation result or equivalent, not another sentinel that can itself appear as an entry. Demonstrate fail-before/pass-after and rerun the full approved DoD before closing this same issue again.

Controller coordination: this is an intentional reopening of an existing scoped issue, not new scope. The active worker on its separate issue is allowed to finish. The driver's closed-set guard is expected to stop at that boundary because this closed issue was reopened by supervision. Add real public-interface regressions for explicit null and a struct with the required registrant_id otherwise valid. Both must return the repository-standard validation tuple without dispatch or exception. Correct the type/omission distinction and safely validate plain string-keyed maps; do not add a broad rescue, silently discard supplied null, or coerce structs. ## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Support all three optional arrays together or separately; deletes are objects containing id, not a bare list of integers.
- [ ] Creates require name/type/content; updates require id and permit name/content/ttl/priority/regions but not type; preserve apex names, zero ttl/priority, empty regions and absent fields.
- [ ] Never split, reorder within arrays, retry a mutation automatically, or emulate this endpoint with individual writes. The server processes deletes, then updates, then creates.
- [ ] Preserve indexed errors for each of creates/updates/deletes, including optional per-field string-array errors; test feature-gated HTTP 412.
- [ ] First add fail-before contract/regression tests for this public interface; after implementation the same tests pass with deterministic offline Req adapters and fake credentials.
- [ ] Assert exact method, bound path, supported query/body fields and one request for the canonical operation. No hidden preflight, follow-up, mutation retry, confirmation prompt, resolver call or network fallback.
- [ ] Cover every documented success status/shape plus applicable nullable/nested fields; malformed successful envelopes and unexpected statuses must return non-raising CORE-002 errors.
- [ ] Cover documented HTTP failures plus representative 401/403/429/500 failures and Req.TransportError(:timeout), retaining endpoint-specific error data and never making a live call.
- [ ] Test omitted versus explicit payload/query values. Preserve valid false, 0, empty strings/arrays/maps and allowed null; invalid required/type/enum/unknown options fail before the adapter without materializing omitted defaults.
- [ ] Add the endpoint-specific fixtures and public call/return examples described here to the resource's tests and module documentation; do not advertise operations that are still absent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Support all three optional arrays together or separately; deletes are objects containing id, not a bare list of integers.
- [ ] Creates require name/type/content; updates require id and permit name/content/ttl/priority/regions but not type; preserve apex names, zero ttl/priority, empty regions and absent fields.
- [ ] Never split, reorder within arrays, retry a mutation automatically, or emulate this endpoint with individual writes. The server processes deletes, then updates, then creates.
- [ ] Preserve indexed errors for each of creates/updates/deletes, including optional per-field string-array errors; test feature-gated HTTP 412.
- [ ] First add fail-before contract/regression tests for this public interface; after implementation the same tests pass with deterministic offline Req adapters and fake credentials.
- [ ] Assert exact method, bound path, supported query/body fields and one request for the canonical operation. No hidden preflight, follow-up, mutation retry, confirmation prompt, resolver call or network fallback.
- [ ] Cover every documented success status/shape plus applicable nullable/nested fields; malformed successful envelopes and unexpected statuses must return non-raising CORE-002 errors.
- [ ] Cover documented HTTP failures plus representative 401/403/429/500 failures and Req.TransportError(:timeout), retaining endpoint-specific error data and never making a live call.
- [ ] Test omitted versus explicit payload/query values. Preserve valid false, 0, empty strings/arrays/maps and allowed null; invalid required/type/enum/unknown options fail before the adapter without materializing omitted defaults.
- [ ] Add the endpoint-specific fixtures and public call/return examples described here to the resource's tests and module documentation; do not advertise operations that are still absent.
- [ ] Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors, the targeted resource test file, full mix test, and mix format --check-formatted. Add no tooling/framework dependency and preserve all existing public success return shapes.
- [ ] Demonstrate a focused regression or request-contract test failing before and passing after.
- [ ] Use offline Req adapters and fake credentials only; no live production or sandbox requests.
- [ ] Run mix compile --warnings-as-errors, targeted tests, the full mix test suite, mix format --check-formatted, and git diff --check.
- [ ] Preserve existing successful public return shapes and update directly related types and documentation.

- Single-record API rewrites, integrated_zones in batch payloads, transactions across zones and a guessed numerical batch-size limit.

Reopened: > *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Confirmed supervision regression: batch path arguments bypass validation

The API-006 approved brief specifies integer account IDs and String.t() zone names, and requires invalid required/type/enum/unknown inputs to fail before the adapter. At 65d8e58 (unchanged by the subsequent documentation-only repair), batch_change/4 validates only attrs and passes both path arguments directly to Req.

The controller reproduced this through the real functions with an offline adapter at example.invalid: valid integer account/string zone arguments correctly reach the adapter, but account "1010" and numeric zone 2020 also reach it instead of returning NimbleOptions.ValidationError. Both invalid-type cases fail; the valid-input control passes. No live API call was made and no library source was edited during reproduction.

Validate both path arguments before request construction/dispatch and add real no-dispatch regression cases for invalid argument types. Preserve one atomic request, the existing nested-body validation, omissions/zero values, typed results, indexed API errors, and caller Req configuration. Reopened: > *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Confirmed supervision regression: optional expires_on is required by the decoder

API-044's approved response contract marks expires_on as required=false and nullable=true, with Date.t() | nil. It also requires preserving documented missing/null fields. At 968ce2b, Domain.decode/1 nevertheless includes "expires_on" in its required map pattern. Subsequent committed Domain source through 9adc0f9 is unchanged. A valid 200 domain payload omitting this optional field therefore returns the generic status-200 error rather than a typed Domain.

The supervisor reproduced this using the exact immutable decoder, date helpers, and struct in an isolated ExUnit VM, exposing only the decoder for the probe. Present-null expiry, omitted trustee, and malformed-date controls behave as expected, but omission of expires_on fails (3/4 passed). No Mix command, live request, or active-worktree source edit was used.

Treat omitted expires_on as nil without relaxing any required field. Add a real offline Domain.get/3 regression for omission of expires_on and for omission together with optional trustee. Preserve explicit null, valid Date-valued expiry, invalid-date errors, state values, timestamps, and existing request/error behavior. Demonstrate failure-before/success-after and all approved DoD gates before closing this same issue again. No new scope or public API is needed.

Expedite this model correction at priority 1 before more domain operations reuse the decoder; existing severity/category/triage labels remain unchanged. The controller has not edited implementation source. If the driver's exact closed-set guard pauses after the active worker finishes, that is the expected consequence of this intentional reopening; reconcile it before resuming and never clear another claim.

Preserve every existing list success shape. Add explicit page-oriented and all-pages interfaces, and establish reusable pagination behavior for the new APIs. Account listing is not paginated and is excluded.

```json
[
  "ReqDnsimple.Zone.list/3, list_page/3, list_all/3",
```

Reopened: > *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Supervision regression: the documentation test forbids campaign completion

At completed commit 889d6aee572e497b16c92f4720789a93065d597b, test/documentation_contract_test.exs:17-20 requires every inventory state, including pending, to occur in the current inventory. This is still present in the latest completed code. After the final approved API operation is implemented, there must be no pending operation, so this assertion makes the final API worker's full suite fail and prevents the approved campaign from completing.

A deterministic isolated ExUnit reproduction passes with the current partial inventory and fails with the same inventory after replacing only pending implementation values with implemented. The reproduction first confirms the exact approved final distribution: 13 existing + 90 implemented + 8 out-of-scope = 111 published operations / 103 scoped operations. It then fails the original assertion specifically because pending is absent. No Mix command, live API request, or active-worktree source edit was used. This is a conclusive local test-contract error, not an environment or network hypothesis.

Required correction: keep documenting the complete status vocabulary, but validate actual operation implementation values semantically against the allowed states rather than requiring every possible state to be populated forever. Add a real regression that accepts a completed scoped inventory with zero pending entries, while retaining partial-inventory and unknown/invalid-state checks. Do not change the approved operation count, fabricate a permanent pending operation, mark excluded work pending, or weaken the final verification requirement. Prove failure-before/success-after and the full approved DoD before closing this same issue again.

Commit provenance note: original commits 73a6f67 and a5a0e05 contain worker session b8303032-7c2c-44d2-87c6-e45919b0d15e after literal backslash-n sequences rather than a normal Git trailer. Preserve existing history (no amend/rebase). Use actual paragraph/newline separation and a proper Copilot-Session trailer on the corrective implementation and tracker commits; no Co-authored-by trailers.

Controller coordination: this is an intentional reopening of an existing scoped issue. The active worker on a separate API issue may finish normally. The driver's closed-set guard is expected to pause at that boundary; the controller will reconcile the exact changes before safe resumption. comments.text:
Reopened: > *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Active rework: reject null and struct extended attributes before HTTP

The implementation exists, but transfer/4 violates its approved optional-but-non-null object input contract. Its extended_attributes schema uses :any, and the shared helper uses nil for both absence and explicit null. Consequently [registrant_id: 11, extended_attributes: nil] reaches the adapter with JSON null instead of returning a local NimbleOptions.ValidationError. Passing URI.parse("https://example.invalid") as extended_attributes crashes with Protocol.UndefinedError because a struct passes is_map but is not Enumerable. Structs do not satisfy the required string-keyed JSON object contract.

Both failures were reproduced through the real register/4 and transfer/4 functions at immutable76dcc39 in an isolated ExUnit VM using only an offline example.invalid adapter. All six valid omission/empty-map/string-keyed-map dispatch controls passed; the four rejection/crash regressions failed (1/5 tests passed). No Mix, active-source edit, real credential, or live HTTP request was used. Registrar source is unchanged through the observed reopening checkpoint. Existing tests cover list/atom-key invalid maps, but not explicit nil or non-Enumerable structs.

Add real public-interface regressions for explicit null and a struct with the required registrant_id otherwise valid. Both must return the repository-standard validation tuple without dispatch or exception. Correct the type/omission distinction and safely validate plain string-keyed maps; do not add a broad rescue, silently discard supplied null, or coerce structs. Preserve omitted attributes, explicit empty maps, supported dynamic values, false flags, zero IDs, exact premium-price strings, all response states and no-retry/no-preflight behavior. Run the focused and full gates.

## Additional active rework: preserve omitted renewal response fields

Independent certificate review found a separate response-decoding defect, now confirmed through the public purchase_letsencrypt_renewal/4 interface. The approved response contract marks all seven Renewal fields optional (required: false) but non-nullable when supplied: id, old_certificate_id, new_certificate_id, state, auto_renew, created_at and updated_at. Missing fields must become nil in the typed struct; explicit JSON null must still be rejected.

The current decode_renewal/1 instead pattern-matches all seven keys. A legitimate HTTP 201 purchase response containing the three IDs, state=new and auto_renew=false, but omitting timestamps, is incorrectly returned as an error. Deleting any one optional field also fails; the test that treats an omitted id as malformed contradicts the approved contract. Renewal.t likewise lacks the required nil alternatives for absent fields.

Confirmed in a fresh isolated offline ExUnit VM at immutable 8b5f5c4. The certificate source blob is unchanged through observed HEAD 2f68955. Reproducer: /home/chgeuer/.copilot/session-state/fbe0ee48-1ca3-4afa-9ef7-5c2021fa7a62/files/reviews/certificate_renewal_optional_fields_test.exs. Result 3/12 passed: the full seven-field control and both negative-control groups (per-field explicit null, invalid types/enums/timestamps) pass; all seven single-field omissions, omission of both timestamps, and the empty data object fail. Every call uses a fake example.invalid adapter; no live purchase, polling, preflight, or shared Mix build was performed.

Add actual public-interface regressions for these valid omissions. Validate each known field when present, preserve nil only for absence, and retain strict explicit-null, type, enum and timestamp rejection. Update Renewal.t to reflect optional fields and correct the inverted missing-id assertion without weakening other malformed-response checks. Preserve distinct purchase/old/new certificate IDs, false values, HTTP 201 success, one-request/no-retry behavior, raw error preservation and all existing request settings. Fulfil this response work AND the separate malformed-keyword request-container rework below before closing bd-3g9. Do not close peers or alter other inventory entries.

## Active rework: reject malformed keyword attribute containers

The implemented `ReqDnsimple.Certificate.purchase_letsencrypt_renewal/5` still raises ArgumentError for malformed attribute lists such as `[:invalid]` and `[{:name}]`. These containers are lists, but are not keyword lists. They reach NimbleOptions, whose Keyword.keys/1 path raises instead of returning the approved local `{:error, %NimbleOptions.ValidationError{}}`. The exception occurs before adapter dispatch; it is not an HTTP or response-decoding failure.

Reproduced through the actual public interface at immutable8059d45 in an isolated ExUnit VM with already-built dependencies and an example.invalid fake adapter. The supervisor checked all11 completed body-taking APIs: all11 valid keyword controls dispatched exactly once; all22 malformed-container cases raised (11/33 passed). For this issue, both malformed cases fail while its corresponding valid control succeeds. Reproducer: /home/chgeuer/.copilot/session-state/fbe0ee48-1ca3-4afa-9ef7-5c2021fa7a62/files/reviews/keyword_container_regression_test.exs. No Mix/shared-build writes, active-source edits, real credentials or live HTTP were used.

Add permanent offline regressions through this public interface for both malformed containers, including zero adapter calls, before fixing it. Validate keyword-list structure with Keyword.keyword?/1 before invoking NimbleOptions or Keyword helpers; reuse appropriate local/shared validation rather than broad rescue, coercion or dropping bad entries. Preserve valid keyword inputs, required-field checks, unknown-option errors, omission/empty/null distinctions, exact payloads, success types, full HTTP/transport errors and the operation-specific no-retry/no-preflight policy. Run focused and full gates.

This is a confirmed instance of a repeated validation pattern, not a new endpoint or scope expansion. All affected existing issues are reopened separately. A shared fix may benefit peers, but claim/close only this issue; do not change peer tracker state or unrelated inventory entries. Each affected public interface still needs its own concrete regression evidence. The original approved contract below remains in force.

The implemented `ReqDnsimple.Registrar.renew/4` still raises ArgumentError for malformed attribute lists such as `[:invalid]` and `[{:name}]`. These containers are lists, but are not keyword lists. They reach NimbleOptions, whose Keyword.keys/1 path raises instead of returning the approved local `{:error, %NimbleOptions.ValidationError{}}`. The exception occurs before adapter dispatch; it is not an HTTP or response-decoding failure.

Reproduced through the actual public interface at immutable8059d45 in an isolated ExUnit VM with already-built dependencies and an example.invalid fake adapter. The supervisor checked all11 completed body-taking APIs: all11 valid keyword controls dispatched exactly once; all22 malformed-container cases raised (11/33 passed). No Mix/shared-build writes, active-source edits, real credentials or live HTTP were used.

Add permanent offline regressions through this public interface for both malformed containers, including zero adapter calls, before fixing it. Validate keyword-list structure with Keyword.keyword?/1 before invoking NimbleOptions or Keyword helpers; reuse appropriate local/shared validation rather than broad rescue, coercion or dropping bad entries. Preserve valid keyword inputs, required-field checks, unknown-option errors, omission/empty/null distinctions, exact payloads, success types, full HTTP/transport errors and the operation-specific no-retry/no-preflight policy.
